words.definition: a piece of work that a teacher gives you to complete
words.example: The teacher set an {assignment}: a piece of work to hand in by Friday.

words.definition: the latest time by which something must be finished
words.example: The {deadline} is noon; work handed in later will not be accepted.

words.definition: careful study to find out facts about something
words.example: Our {research} into local history involved reading records and interviewing residents.

words.definition: a person, book or place from which information comes
words.example: Every fact needs a {source}, such as a book, interview or official record.

words.definition: a simple drawing that explains how something works
words.example: This labelled {diagram} shows how water moves through a plant.

words.definition: a scientific test to find out what happens
words.example: We designed an {experiment} with two seed trays to test how light affects growth.

words.definition: what happens or is found at the end of a test, race or match
words.example: The race {result} confirmed that Maya finished first.

words.definition: a talk in which someone explains something to a group
words.example: My {presentation} includes slides that I explain aloud to the class.

words.definition: comments about your work that help you make it better
words.example: Helpful {feedback} tells you what worked well and how to improve your work.

words.definition: an official record showing you have passed a course or test
words.example: Passing this course earns a {qualification} that proves you can teach swimming.

words.definition: what someone thinks or believes about something
words.example: Whether winter is best is a matter of {opinion}, not a provable fact.

words.definition: something that explains why you do or believe something
words.example: My {reason} for staying indoors is that I feel ill.

words.definition: facts or objects that help show whether something is true
words.example: The muddy footprints are {evidence} that someone walked through the garden.

words.definition: something good that makes one choice better than another
words.example: One {advantage} of walking is that it costs nothing.

words.definition: something bad that makes one choice less useful
words.example: One {disadvantage} of cycling here is the lack of safe cycle lanes.

words.definition: something known to be true rather than just believed
words.example: It is a {fact} that a triangle has three sides.

words.definition: a particular thing used to show what a larger group is like
words.example: A robin is one {example} of a bird that lives in gardens.

words.definition: the act of picking between two or more possibilities
words.example: With soup or salad available, I have a {choice} of two starters.

words.definition: a way of dealing successfully with a problem
words.example: Adding a ramp is a {solution} to the problem of wheelchair access.

words.definition: the final judgement reached after thinking about information
words.example: After studying the evidence, we reached a {conclusion} about which route saves time.

words.definition: to have the same view as someone else
words.example: We both think the plan is good, so I {agree} with you.

words.definition: to have a different view from someone else
words.example: I {disagree} with your answer: I think the total should be twelve.

words.definition: to put forward an idea for people to think about
words.example: Please {suggest} a name to the editor, who needs ideas for our newspaper.

words.definition: to like one thing more than another
words.example: I {prefer} cycling to driving because I enjoy the fresh air.

words.definition: to look at things together to find similarities and differences
words.example: We {compare} the two maps to find what has changed between them.

words.definition: to help show that an idea or statement is true
words.example: The results {support} our idea, although more evidence is needed to prove it.

words.definition: to make someone decide to do something by giving reasons
words.example: We hope to {persuade} the council to add bins by explaining the need.

words.definition: to say something is true even when others may doubt it
words.example: They {claim} to own this castle, although no evidence of ownership has been shown.

words.definition: to show certainly that something is true
words.example: These dated photographs {prove}, beyond any doubt, that the bridge existed before 1900.

words.definition: to think carefully about something before making a decision
words.example: I will {consider} whether to accept, thinking carefully before I decide.

words.definition: used to introduce something that makes the next fact surprising
words.example: I enjoyed the walk, {although} it rained the whole way.

words.definition: used to introduce a different or surprising point
words.example: The tiny room, {however}, felt spacious, contrary to what its size suggested.

words.definition: for that reason, as a result of what was just said
words.example: The bus cannot move without fuel; {therefore}, its empty tank prevents departure.

words.definition: except if a particular thing happens
words.example: We cannot enter {unless} someone unlocks the door for us.

words.definition: used when asking or deciding between possibilities
words.example: We must decide {whether} to walk or take the bus.

words.definition: without being prevented by something
words.example: We stayed dry {despite} the rain, thanks to our waterproof coats.

words.definition: in place of someone or something else
words.example: There was no rice, so we cooked pasta {instead}.

words.definition: used to add another point or piece of information
words.example: The hostel provides breakfast; {in addition}, guests can use bicycles for free.

words.definition: used before one thing that shows what you mean
words.example: Some mammals lay eggs; {for instance}, the duck-billed platypus does.

words.definition: used to introduce the opposite side of a situation
words.example: On the one hand, flying is quicker; {on the other hand}, trains pollute less.

words.definition: a piece of equipment made for a particular purpose
words.example: A tablet is a portable electronic {device} with a touchscreen.

words.definition: the programs that tell a computer what to do
words.example: This drawing {software} must be installed before the computer can open pictures.

words.definition: a joining that allows devices to exchange information
words.example: Without an internet {connection}, this tablet cannot send messages online.

words.definition: a service that finds web pages from words you enter
words.example: I type keywords into a {search engine} to find relevant web pages.

words.definition: a file sent together with an email
words.example: The photograph came as an email {attachment} that I opened separately.

words.definition: being able to keep personal things away from other people
words.example: Closing the curtains gives us {privacy} so people outside cannot watch us.

words.definition: agreement that allows someone to do something
words.example: You need the owner's {permission} to enter; she must first say you may.

words.definition: to add the newest changes to something
words.example: We {update} the computer's software to install the latest fixes.

words.definition: to join a device to another device or a network
words.example: Use this cable to {connect} the printer to the computer.

words.definition: to let other people see or use something you have
words.example: I {share} my private notes with one friend, without making them public.

words.definition: a place where you stay or live
words.example: Our holiday {accommodation} is a cottage with three bedrooms and a kitchen.

words.definition: a plan listing the places and times of a journey
words.example: Our {itinerary} lists each city we will visit and when we leave.

words.definition: a machine used to carry people or goods on land
words.example: A van is a road {vehicle} used to carry people or goods.

words.definition: a person travelling on foot
words.example: A {pedestrian} is walking across the road, so the driver stops.

words.definition: a marked place where people can go across a road
words.example: Wait at the zebra {crossing} until the cars stop for you.

words.definition: the act of travelling from one place to another
words.example: The train {journey} from here to London takes two hours.

words.definition: the amount of space between two places
words.example: Use the map's scale to calculate the {distance} in kilometres between these villages.

words.definition: the way towards which someone or something moves
words.example: The arrow points north, showing the {direction} we must walk.

words.definition: to decide that something planned will not happen
words.example: We must {cancel} the trip completely, so it will not happen at all.

words.definition: to get onto a ship, aircraft, train or bus
words.example: Passengers will {board} the aircraft through gate seven when their group is called.

words.definition: steady because your weight is spread evenly
words.example: In yoga, I stay {balanced} by keeping my weight equal on both feet.

words.definition: containing things your body needs to grow and stay well
words.example: Lentils are {nutritious}, providing protein and other things our bodies need.

words.definition: a condition where something normally harmless makes your body react badly
words.example: My nut {allergy} means eating peanuts can make me seriously ill.

words.definition: an illness caused by tiny living things entering the body
words.example: The doctor says germs have caused an {infection} in my ear.

words.definition: the way you hold your body when sitting or standing
words.example: Sitting with a straight back helps me keep good {posture}.

words.definition: a feeling of worry caused by difficult demands
words.example: Too many deadlines at once can cause {stress} and make relaxation difficult.

words.definition: a usual order of things you do regularly
words.example: My evening {routine} is the usual order: homework, dinner, then brushing my teeth.

words.definition: something you do often, sometimes without thinking
words.example: Without noticing, I bit my nails again; it's a {habit} I cannot break.

words.definition: to keep away from something or stop it happening
words.example: To {avoid} the puddle, I walk around it instead of through it.

words.definition: to become calm and less worried
words.example: I listen to gentle music to {relax} and let my worries go.

words.definition: the usual weather in a place over many years
words.example: The desert's {climate} is usually hot and dry, year after year.

words.definition: a statement about what the weather is likely to be
words.example: Tomorrow's weather {forecast} predicts rain and strong winds.

words.definition: gases sent out into the air by machines or processes
words.example: Car exhaust {emissions} include gases that warm the planet.

words.definition: something useful that people can use to meet their needs
words.example: Fresh water is a natural {resource} that people need for drinking and farming.

words.definition: a group of living things of the same kind
words.example: A red fox and an Arctic fox belong to different {species}.

words.definition: at risk of disappearing completely as a kind of animal or plant
words.example: These turtles are {endangered}; so few remain that they could disappear completely.

words.definition: coming from a supply that nature can replace
words.example: Wind provides {renewable} energy because using it does not use it up.

words.definition: to use carefully so that supplies will last
words.example: We {conserve} water by collecting rain to use on the garden.

words.definition: to harm something so that it works less well or looks worse
words.example: Heavy boots can {damage} delicate plants by crushing their leaves.

words.definition: to use something again, perhaps for a different purpose
words.example: We {reuse} empty jam jars as containers for pencils.

words.definition: a programme sent out by radio or television
words.example: We listened to the live radio {broadcast} of the match.

words.definition: a piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or website
words.example: I read a newspaper {article} with a headline and six paragraphs about the concert.

words.definition: the person who checks and chooses material for publication
words.example: The magazine's {editor} decides which stories will appear in the next issue.

words.definition: someone whose job is to gather and tell news
words.example: The {reporter} stood outside the town hall to tell viewers the news.

words.definition: a short piece of writing that explains a picture
words.example: The {caption} below the photograph names the people shown in it.

words.definition: a line of text showing what someone says in a film
words.example: Each {subtitle} translates one spoken line of the foreign-language film into English.

words.definition: to make writing or pictures available for people to read
words.example: They {publish} a monthly magazine, printing copies for sale in shops.

words.definition: to tell people something officially or publicly
words.example: The head teacher will {announce} the winner over the loudspeaker at noon.

words.definition: to say what someone or something is like
words.example: Please {describe} the missing bag, including its colour, shape and size.

words.definition: to give the main points without all the details
words.example: Please {summarise} the article, giving only its main points rather than every detail.

words.definition: sure that you can do something well
words.example: After many successful rehearsals, I feel {confident} that I can perform well.

words.definition: able to be trusted to do what is needed
words.example: My {reliable} alarm clock has worked perfectly every morning for ten years.

words.definition: having the duty of taking care of something
words.example: I am {responsible} for feeding the rabbit; that job is mine.

words.definition: able to do things without needing other people's help
words.example: She is financially {independent} of her parents because she earns her own money.

words.definition: wanting great success, or needing a lot of work to succeed
words.example: His {ambitious} target is to double our school's recycling total in one month.

words.definition: wanting to learn or find out more
words.example: A {curious} child keeps asking how things work and why.

words.definition: unwilling to change your mind even when others give good reasons
words.example: He is so {stubborn} that no amount of reasoning changes his mind.

words.definition: speaking a lot
words.example: He is so {talkative} that he rarely stops speaking long enough to listen.

words.definition: worried that something bad may happen
words.example: I feel {anxious} about the test and cannot stop worrying about it.

words.definition: feeling bad because you have done something wrong
words.example: I felt {ashamed} of cheating and wished I had acted honestly.

words.definition: a person who chooses to help without being paid
words.example: Each {volunteer} helps at the food bank without receiving any pay.

words.definition: an organisation that helps people or causes in need
words.example: This registered {charity} uses donated money to help families who cannot afford food.

words.definition: people who live in one area or share something
words.example: Our village {community} includes everyone who lives here, young and old.

words.definition: a small group chosen to organise or decide things
words.example: The elected {committee} of six pupils meets to make decisions for the whole club.

words.definition: organised activities intended to achieve a particular change
words.example: We launched a {campaign} of petitions and posters to demand safer streets.

words.definition: to work together to achieve something
words.example: We {cooperate} by combining our efforts rather than competing against one another.

words.definition: to plan and arrange the parts of an event or activity
words.example: I will {organise} the concert, arranging performers, tickets and rehearsal times.

words.definition: to give something to help a person or cause
words.example: We {donate} spare blankets to the shelter without expecting anything back.

words.definition: to make someone or something part of a group or activity
words.example: Please {include} me in the team rather than leaving me out.

words.definition: to split something into smaller parts or groups
words.example: We {divide} the cake into six equal slices, one for each guest.

words.definition: the need to deal with one thing before others
words.example: Homework takes {priority} over games because it must be finished before tomorrow.

words.definition: something you are trying to achieve
words.example: After months of training, I reached my {goal} of swimming a kilometre without stopping.

words.definition: movement towards a better or more complete state
words.example: I have made {progress} in reading: I can now finish books without help.

words.definition: the hard work needed to do something
words.example: Learning this difficult piece took a lot of {effort} and many practice sessions.

words.definition: a chance to do something you want to do
words.example: Winning the only available place gave me an {opportunity} to learn violin.

words.definition: to practise a performance before an audience comes to see it
words.example: Actors {rehearse} by performing the play in an empty theatre before opening night.

words.definition: to succeed in doing something you have worked towards
words.example: With hard work, I hope to {achieve} excellent marks in my final exams.

words.definition: to move a planned event to a later time
words.example: We will {postpone} Monday's meeting until Wednesday, two days later.

words.definition: to sleep longer than planned and wake up too late
words.example: I {oversleep} when my alarm fails and I wake later than planned.

words.definition: often, with similar amounts of time between occasions
words.example: I practise {regularly}, every Monday and Thursday without missing a session.
